nodes.name: Solution phase reduction
nodes.procedure: The fccx Ru–Sn nanoflowers were prepared using a solution phase reduction strategy by adding RuCl3·xH2O and a certain amount of Sn(CH3COO)2 into oleylamine (Fig. 1a). Note that the ratio of the Ru–Sn fcc phase was modulated by varying the amount of Sn(CH3COO)2, namely, fcc0.25 Ru–Sn, fcc0.42 Ru–Sn, fcc0.63 Ru–Sn, and fcc Ru–Sn (details are provided in the Experimental section). In the absence of Sn(CH3COO)2, the obtained Ru nanobranches appear in the hcp phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp Ru shows characteristic peaks at 38.3°, 42.1°, and 43.5° (PDF: 88–1734). fccx Ru–Sn shows gradual weakening of hcp peaks and strengthening of fcc peaks. Rietveld refinement gives fcc/hcp ratios of 0.25/0.75, 0.42/0.58, and 0.63/0.37. fcc Ru–Sn shows SnO2 peaks due to oxidation of high Sn content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the absence of Sn(CH3COO)2, the obtained Ru nanobranches appear in the hcp phase (PDF: 88–1734), as indicated by the characteristic peaks at 38.3°, 42.1°, and 43.5° in the X-ray diffraction (XRD, Fig. 1b) pattern ... the presence of SnO2 peaks in the XRD pattern of fcc Ru–Sn can be attributed to the oxidation of Sn with a high content.

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp Ru shows nanobranch morphology. fccx Ru–Sn shows morphological transformation to nanoflowers with mean size ~30 nm for fcc0.42 Ru–Sn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show the nanobranch morphology of hcp Ru ... After introducing Sn(CH3COO)2, the nanobranches become blunted, resulting in the morphological transformation of fccx Ru–Sn into nanoflowers (Fig. 1e and Fig. S7 and S8, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp Ru: lattice distance 0.215 nm for (002) plane. fcc0.42 Ru–Sn: lattice distances 0.217 nm for hcp (002) and 0.223 nm for fcc (111), confirming heterointerface. False color HRTEM, FFT, and IFFT validate fcc/hcp boundary.
nodes.evidence_snippet: with a lattice distance of 0.215 nm in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image corresponding to the (002) plane of hcp Ru (Fig. S6, ESI†) ... The lattice distances of 0.217 nm and 0.223 nm in the HRTEM images can be indexed as the (002) facet of the hcp phase and the (111) facet of the fcc phase, respectively, further confirming the existence of heterointerfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru and Sn are evenly distributed on fcc0.42 Ru–Sn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, Ru and Sn are evenly distributed on fcc0.42 Ru–Sn as shown by the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) maps (Fig. 1j).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru loading content determined for fccx Ru–Sn/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru loading content was determined with thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) (Fig. S10, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C: Negative shift of Ru 3p peak and positive shift of Sn 3d peak indicate electron transfer from Sn to Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) reveals that the introduction of Sn leads to the electron transfer from Sn to Ru, as evidenced by the negative shift of the Ru 3p peak (Fig. 3a) and the positive shift of the Sn 3d peak (Fig. 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES: fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C and hcp Ru/C close to Ru foil (metallic Ru), fcc0.42 slightly lower energy position due to electron transfer from Sn. Sn K-edge XANES: fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C edge position between Sn foil and SnO2 (oxidative Sn state).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3c, the peak positions of Ru K-edge for fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C and hcp Ru/C are close to that of the Ru foil, suggesting that Ru in fcc0.4 Ru–Sn/C and hcp Ru/C is predominantly present as the metallic state. Compared to hcp Ru/C, the energy position of Ru K-edge for fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C is slightly lower ... In the Sn K-edge XANES spectra, the edge position of fcc Ru–Sn/C locates between the Sn foil and SnO2, which suggests that Sn in fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C present as the oxidative state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS: Ru–Ru coordination number (CN) ~4.1 for fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C (lower than ~4.9 for hcp Ru/C), indicating unsaturated Ru coordination. Sn K-edge EXAFS: Sn–Ru coordination peak at 2.41 Å with CN ~1.8.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Detailed fitting of the EXAFS spectra shows that the coordination number (CN) of Ru–Ru for fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C is ∼4.1, which is lower than that for hcp Ru/C (4.9), suggesting the unsaturated coordination state of Ru in fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C ... CN of Sn–Ru was estimated to be ∼1.8.

nodes.characterization_summary: fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C: main H2 desorption peak at ~408°C (vs 412°C for hcp Ru/C), indicating weaker H2 adsorption; additional peaks at 268°C and 312°C from moderate H2 adsorption on Sn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the H2-TPD curve of fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C, the main H2 desorption peak locates at ~408°C, which is slightly lower than that of hcp Ru/C (412°C), indicating its weaker adsorption towards H2 compared to hcp Ru/C ... The peaks present at 268°C and 312°C in the H2-TPD curve of fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C are attributed to the moderate H2 adsorption on Sn.

nodes.characterization_summary: fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C: CO linear adsorption ~2108 cm⁻¹ and bridged adsorption ~1930 cm⁻¹ with lower peak intensities than Pt/C; larger wavenumber shift slopes (linear: 29.4 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹, bridge: 96.3 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹ vs Pt/C: 23.4 and 56.8 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹), indicating weaker CO adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C, the peaks at ~2108 cm⁻¹ and ~1930 cm⁻¹ in the IR spectrum can be assigned as CO linear adsorption and bridged adsorption, respectively ... both the slopes of fcc0.42 Ru–Sn/C for CO linear adsorption (29.4 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹) and bridge adsorption (96.3 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹) are obviously larger than those of Pt/C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu underpotential deposition (Cu UPD) stripping used to measure electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) for specific activity normalization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the specific activity (j0,s) normalized by the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) was measured using their underpotential deposited Cu (Cu UPD) stripping experiment (Fig. S14, ESI†).
